title: Freight broker surety bonds: BMC-84, BMC-85 and claims
seoTitle: Freight Broker Bonds: BMC-84, BMC-85 & Claims
searchIntent: What does a freight broker bond cover and how do claims work?
excerpt: Understand freight broker financial security, the difference between a bond and trust, and the documentation to gather before pursuing a claim.
takeaway: Financial security is not general business insurance or a promise that every disputed invoice will be paid. Understand the instrument and document the underlying obligation.

sections.title: Distinguish a bond from a trust and insurance
paragraphs: Luis’s lessons explain why brokers need to understand financial security before a payment dispute occurs. FMCSA identifies BMC-84 surety bonds and BMC-85 trust fund agreements as ways to meet the applicable $75,000 financial-security requirement.

A surety arrangement is not the same as holding that amount as operating cash. Nor should a broker treat a bond as insurance that makes unpaid obligations disappear. Reimbursement obligations may apply under the surety agreement.

sections.title: Separate the shipment dispute from the claim process
paragraphs: Before escalating, establish what was agreed, what work was performed, what was billed and why payment remains outstanding. Luis describes a situation in which an invoice had been missed in a spam folder; direct contact can sometimes identify an administrative problem.

That does not mean every overdue balance is an innocent mistake. It means the collection record should show reasonable attempts to reach the correct billing contact and resolve missing documents or a stated dispute.

sections.title: Identify the correct business and provider
paragraphs: Confirm the legal business you contracted with and its relevant registration information. Use official records and independently verified contacts to identify the financial-security provider rather than relying solely on a name in an email.
Ask the provider for its current claim procedure and required documentation. Do not assume that a process shown in an older video still uses the same form, address or submission method.

sections.title: Assemble evidence of the obligation
paragraphs: Keep a clear chronology and the documents that support it. The purpose is to make the transaction understandable to someone who did not arrange the shipment.
bullets: The agreement and rate confirmation, including relevant terms.
Shipment and delivery records, including the signed proof of delivery where applicable.
The invoice and evidence of submission.
Collection correspondence, responses and the explanation of any dispute.

sections.title: Account for current financial-responsibility rules
paragraphs: FMCSA’s financial-responsibility changes effective January 16, 2026 include rules affecting eligible trust assets and action when available financial security falls below the required amount. Its current compliance guidance should be consulted instead of historical descriptions of the system.

A claim may involve disputed facts or competing obligations. Neither this article nor the existence of financial security guarantees a particular recovery. Seek appropriate advice when the amount or disagreement warrants it.

sections.title: Use prevention alongside escalation
paragraphs: Accurate billing contacts, complete paperwork, credit controls and consistent collection follow-up remain important even where financial security exists. Keep payment responsibilities clear before freight moves.

For brokers, read the surety or trust agreement and understand the obligations it creates. For claimants, preserve evidence and follow the provider’s current process. A unilateral edit to paperwork should not be assumed to bind another party.
